reviews.quote: The Asus Chromebook Plus CX34 proves that budget-friendly Chromebooks have more to offer than ever before, with more performance and even better features. Editors' Choice.
Asus Chromebook Plus CX34 review: a simple, smart purchase - ChromeOS is really good at simplifying.
A powerful, reasonably priced everyday laptop with zippy, reliable performance and just over 12 hours of battery life.

praises: i5-1334U + 16GB + 512GB at $699.97 is the highest x86 spec you can buy on ChromeOS in Canada — headroom for years
CX34 chassis is the best-built budget Chromebook: rigid deck, good hinge, backlit keyboard
Touchscreen plus 1080p webcam plus microSD — the practical extras the cheap SKUs skip
12 months of Google AI Pro bundled (per listing) — real value on top of the machine
Iris Xe handles Linux-container dev tools and heavy tab loads far better than N-series Chromebooks
complaints: Still ChromeOS at $700 — buyers who later need desktop apps are stuck
16GB RAM is soldered; the 512GB is the only reason to pick this tier over cheaper ones
Glossy touch panel reflects light and is class-typical ~45% NTSC colour
13th-gen Intel (2023) is aging in a 2026 listing; newer N-series twins are more efficient
No active pen support despite the touchscreen

standouts: Best raw spec-per-dollar in the CA Chromebook inventory: 16GB/512GB + i5 + touch + backlit keyboard at $699.97 with 12mo Google AI Pro
design_philosophy: ASUS's CX34 is the 'spec-maxxing' Chromebook Plus: instead of cutting hardware to hold a price, it packs a full 13th-gen Core i5, 16GB RAM, and 512GB storage into a well-built touch chassis at just under $700. The bet is that Chromebook buyers keep machines ~6 years (the update window), so CPU/RAM headroom is worth more than thinness.
